changes.before: Define ShelfKey as shown and uniqueShelfCount(_:) to return the number of distinct room/shelf pairs in an array.
changes.after: Let a set recognize matching values made from your own type.

before: Equatable provides meaningful == comparisons. Hashable also supplies hashing for sets and dictionary keys and includes the equality requirement. Swift can synthesize both for this struct because its stored String and Int fields already support them. Equality compares all stored fields; a different field makes a different key.

ShelfKey(room:shelf:) constructs the value. Set<ShelfKey> stores distinct keys; equal a and same occupy one entry. keys.contains(same) asks membership and returns Bool. Equal values must have matching hashes, but matching hashes do not prove equality: collisions are allowed. Do not print or assert a particular hash number; hashing is intentionally not a stable saved identifier. These keys have constant stored fields and no shared mutable references.

Follow this complete example.
```swift
struct ShelfKey: Hashable {
    let room: String
    let shelf: Int
}
let a = ShelfKey(room: "east", shelf: 2)
let same = ShelfKey(room: "east", shelf: 2)
let different = ShelfKey(room: "east", shelf: 3)
let keys: Set<ShelfKey> = [a, same, different]
print(a == same)
print(a == different)
print(keys.count)
print(keys.contains(same))
```
Output:
```text
true
false
2
true
```

Change the input or declaration and trace the result.
```swift

    let shelf: Int
}
let a = ShelfKey(room: "east", shelf: 2)
let same = ShelfKey(room: "east", shelf: 2)
let different = ShelfKey(room: "west", shelf: 2)
let keys: Set<ShelfKey> = [a, same, different]
print(a == same)
print(a == different)
print(keys.count)
print(keys.contains(same))
```
Output:
```text
true
false
2
true
```
after: A ShelfKey identifies one shelf in one room. Two keys are equal only when both their room and shelf match. Swift can create that equality check from the stored properties.

Hashable lets a type work in a Set or as dictionary keys. It includes Equatable, which supports == comparisons. Because String and Int already support Hashable, Swift can build the needed behavior for this simple struct.

A hash is a number that helps a set find values quickly. Equal values need matching hashes, but unequal values can also have matching hashes. The set still checks equality. Hashes can change between program runs, so do not save one as a permanent ID.
Keep ShelfKey as shown. Complete uniqueShelfCount(_:) to count different room-and-shelf pairs in an array. Set(keys) removes repeated keys, and .count gives the total. An empty array gives zero.
